when: between about 3:15 and 4:30 and you are level 4
asks: where do I go now
first clear's done what next
camps are gone what do I do
what's my next move
say: Your first camps come back soonest, so restart there for steady levels, or gank the nearest lane now while nothing of yours is up.
more: Small camps return about two and a quarter minutes after you kill them, so the order you cleared in is the order they come back.
Buffs take five minutes, so this second clear is small camps only. That's why a gank right now costs you so little.
Farming gets you toward six sooner. The gank can win a lane that later moves first for dragon or grubs.
check: Which of your camps have actually respawned, where the nearest wave is, and whether that laner has health to follow up.
breaks: If the nearest lane is pushed up to their tower there is no gank; walk to the camp that returns first, or take a crab if one is alive.
basis: pro:Gank when your camps are down

asks: when's my buff back
how long till red respawns
are my buffs up yet
when do camps come back
say: Buffs come back five minutes after you took them and small camps in about two and a quarter, so farm small camps or gank until then.
more: A buff taken in the first clear is due somewhere between about six and eight minutes, depending on when you killed it.
That makes the second clear a small-camp clear: gromp, wolves, raptors and krugs, in the order you killed them.
Plan the third clear to start on the buff that returns first, so you carry it into the grubs window at eight minutes.
check: The time you killed each buff, and the respawn timers shown on your own map.
breaks: If their jungler took one of your buffs, its timer runs from his kill, not yours; go by the timer on the map rather than your own route.

when: you are level 4 or 5, before 6:00
asks: which side should I clear toward
top side or bot side second clear
what lane do I play for
where should my clear end
say: End this clear beside the lane you want to gank and go straight in, or start on that side if you're recalling after.
more: If you gank straight from your last camp, finishing next to that lane saves the walk.
If you recall instead, you come back to the camps you cleared first, so those are the ones that should sit beside the lane you care about.
Their jungler has the same problem. If he clears one side and recalls, he is pulled away from it for a while.
Pick the lane that can carry or the one that can be ganked. Those are not always the same lane.
check: Which lane has a wave you can gank into, which laner has their spells, and which of your camps are up.
breaks: If the lane you wanted is already lost and pushed under tower, playing toward it feeds their jungler; switch to the other side.
basis: pro:End the clear beside the lane that matters

when: you are at least one level above their jungler
asks: I'm a level up on their jungler what now
I'm ahead in jungle where do I go
should I invade him
how do I use my level lead
say: With the level lead, wait at the camp or crab he still needs and fight him there, or keep clearing your own side to widen it.
more: A jungler who is behind has very few safe places to farm, so his next stop is easy to guess.
Meeting him there denies the camp and may get the kill. Clearing instead is slower but carries no risk.
Either way, take your own camps on time. A level lead disappears quickly if you spend a minute hovering for nothing.
check: Which of his camps and which crab are still alive, and whether his nearest laner can walk over before yours.
breaks: If his mid or side laner has push and yours does not, the invade turns into a two on one; stay on your own camps.
basis: pro:A jungler who is behind has few places to go

when: their jungler is at least one level above you
asks: their jungler is ahead of me
I'm behind in levels where do I farm
he keeps invading me
I'm down a level what now
say: You're down a level, so farm the side he isn't on and gank from there, or sit near a lane that can protect your camps.
more: He expects you at your most obvious camp. Taking the far side, or the one beside a strong lane, is how you get farm without a fight.
Don't try to match him in river. A level this early is stats and sometimes an ability rank.
A couple of quiet clears is how the gap closes, and your ganks still work if the laner brings the damage.
check: Where he was last seen, which of your camps are up, and which of your lanes is pushing.
breaks: If he shows on the far side of the map, the rule flips; take everything near you and gank the lane he just left.
basis: pro:A jungler who is behind has few places to go

when: one of your side laners is well behind their lane opponent in CS or level
asks: my top is losing do I go help
bot lane's getting smashed where do I path
should I path to the losing lane
is that side of my jungle safe
say: The jungle beside a losing lane isn't safe, so clear the other half with lanes that can move, or cover that lane only for a dive.
more: Their laner arrives first to anything near that lane, so fights in that quadrant start with you outnumbered.
You give a camp or two there. In return you keep your life and get real ganks on the side where your laners can follow.
Come back to that side when the wave is under your tower and they overstay. That is the moment a counter-gank pays.
check: Whether that wave is under your tower right now, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If the losing laner is your team's only carry, giving the whole side loses the game slowly; hold near them for the dive instead.
basis: pro:The jungle beside a losing lane is theirs

when: their jungler is dead with a respawn timer
asks: their jungler just died what do I do
enemy jungle is dead where do I go
he's dead should I invade
can I take his camps
say: He's dead, so walk into his jungle and take whatever is up, or start an objective right now if one is alive.
more: With him dead there is no Smite against you and no counter-gank, for as long as that timer runs.
His camps put you further ahead for the six race. An objective is worth more if your lanes can reach it.
Leave before he respawns and walks back. His laners get there first, so the second camp is the greedy one.
check: How long his timer is, which of his camps are alive, and whether a dragon or crab is up.
breaks: If your own health is low after the fight, his laners can kill you in there; recall and spend the gold instead.
basis: pro:A dead jungler makes the objective free

when: you are dead or just respawned, before 8:00
asks: I just died where do I go
died in jungle what now
how do I recover after dying
what do I do when I respawn
say: Spend your gold, then go straight to the camp that respawned first for safe levels, or cover a lane if their jungler is diving it.
more: While you were dead he had free time. Assume he took a crab or one of your camps and plan around what's left.
A calm clear costs you nothing more. Forcing a gank to make up for the death is how one death becomes two.
Keep an eye on his level. If he reaches six before you, stay out of river until you catch up.
check: Which of your camps are still alive, and where their jungler showed while you were dead.
breaks: If he is clearly on the far side, a gank on the near lane is free; take it instead of walking past it to a camp.
basis: pro:A jungler who is behind has few places to go

when: their jungler took part in a kill on a side laner in the last 20 seconds
asks: he just ganked top what do I do
their jungler showed bot
enemy jungler is other side
he's top side can I go
say: He just showed in that lane, so if you're on the other side, gank there with no counter-gank, or take his camps near you.
more: A sighting is a short window. It lasts about as long as it takes him to walk back across the map.
The gank gets a lane ahead. His camps get you ahead. Pick the gank if the wave is near your tower.
Tell the lane he left that they can trade forward for a moment too.
check: Whether that lane is the far side from you, how long ago he showed, and whether your near lane's wave lets you reach the target.
breaks: If the sighting is more than a few seconds old or he recalled after it, treat him as unseen and take only what's close.
basis: pro:A jungler seen on the far side opens yours

asks: should I just farm
do I gank or keep clearing
is it fine to full clear again
I scale should I afk farm
say: You scale on camps, so keep full clearing toward six, or gank only when a lane is on your route and already winning the trade.
more: Your champion gets more from two clean clears than from one hopeful gank, and the level six race is yours to win that way.
The cost is that your lanes play alone for a few minutes, so ping them when their jungler is missing.
A lane that needs no help to kill is the exception. Those ganks are short and you lose almost no camps.
check: Whether your camps are up, and whether any lane is being dived while you farm.
breaks: If their jungler is living in one of your lanes, another clear loses that lane; cover it once, then go back to farming.

when: you are level 4 or 5, between about 3:15 and 5:30
asks: I'm an early ganker where now
who do I gank
my camps are down which lane
second gank where
say: This is your strongest stretch, so gank the lane pushed toward your tower while camps are down, or invade if their jungler is weaker early.
more: Your champion's edge is these minutes. Each one spent waiting for camps is an edge you don't get back.
A kill now is gold for a component before their jungler has his. That is the item you bring to the next river fight.
If neither is on, take the crab side with your stronger lanes and reset.
check: Whether your camps really are down, where each wave is, which enemy laner used Flash, and which of your laners has health.
breaks: If every lane is pushed to their tower, forcing a gank burns the window anyway; take a camp of his or recall for an item.
basis: pro:Gank when your camps are down

asks: I've been waiting in this bush forever
the gank isn't happening do I leave
how long do I wait for a gank
should I keep hovering this lane
say: If the gank hasn't started by the time the next wave arrives, leave for the camp that's back first, or recall if you hold gold.
more: Every second in the bush comes out of your camp timers. The jungler already on his camps is also first to the next river fight.
Staying only pays if the wave is about to turn your way. If their cover has arrived, it won't.
Leaving early loses nothing. The lane is still there next clear.
check: Whether their jungler or support has shown up to cover, where the wave is, and which camp of yours is back.
breaks: If the laner is about to crash a big wave for a dive and you're already there, the extra few seconds are worth it.
basis: pro:Hovering a play that never starts costs the next clear

asks: my gank failed again
should I gank that lane again
he keeps getting away
do I go back top again
say: If that lane's escaped twice, put your time into another lane or your camps, or go back only if the last try burned his Flash.
more: Some champions are simply safe near their tower. A well-reasoned gank still fails on them.
Each failed try hands their jungler free time on the other side.
A burned Flash changes it. Come back within the next couple of clears while it's still down.
check: How many times you've tried that lane, whether Flash or an escape was used last time, and where that wave sits now.
breaks: If your laner has since hit six and has lockdown of their own, the lane is worth one more visit.
basis: pro:Stop repeating a gank that keeps failing

when: you just got a kill or assist in a lane before 8:00
asks: got the kill what now
gank worked where do I go
do I help push after the kill
we killed bot what next
say: Help shove the wave into tower so the kill turns into lost minions for them, or leave at once if a camp of yours is up.
more: A kill only counts as a lead if the farm goes your way too. A crashed wave makes the dead laner miss gold and experience.
Shoving also lets your laner recall safely or walk with you to the crab or dragon.
If you hold enough gold for a component, recall after the shove and bring it to the next fight.
check: How big the wave is, whether your laner wants the minions, and which of your camps is back.
breaks: If their jungler is still alive nearby and you're both low, shoving invites the counter-gank; back off and recall.
basis: pro:After a won fight, the waves decide whether you got paid

when: between about 6:00 and 7:30
asks: where do I clear before grubs
how do I path for eight minutes
third clear which side
setting up for grubs
say: Clear bot side first and finish top side just before eight for grubs, or reverse it if your team would rather take dragon.
more: You want your last camps to die near the objective you plan to take, so you arrive on time without leaving farm behind.
Grubs are one window from eight minutes and don't come back, so decide now whether you are taking them or trading for dragon.
Buffs from the first clear return around now. Starting on one means you carry it into that fight.
check: Which buffs are back, which of your lanes can leave their wave at eight, and where their jungler last showed.
breaks: If top lane is losing hard, grubs are a fight you arrive second to; path bot and take the dragon as the trade.

asks: I flashed early what do I do
no flash should I still gank
my flash is down where do I go
used flash in the invade
say: Without Flash, farm two full clears while it comes back, or gank only lanes where the laner supplies the lockdown.
more: An early lost Flash takes away most play-making for a few minutes. Farming junglers lose the least from it.
About two full clears cover most of the cooldown, and you come out level with a jungler who spent that time ganking.
Stay away from deep river on your own until it's back.
check: When you used Flash, and whether your champion truly needs it to reach a target.
breaks: If their jungler is the one without Flash, do the opposite; these are your minutes to invade or gank.
basis: pro:Without Flash, a farming jungler clears it back

when: you have more kills or assists than their jungler but less CS
asks: I have kills but he has more farm
am I actually ahead
he's out-farming me
I'm up kills down cs
say: Your kills cost you camps, so full clear now to bank the lead, or keep ganking only if a lane is one kill from snowballing.
more: Count camps and items, not the kill column. A jungler up kills but down a level is not ahead in a duel.
He has been farming toward six while you ganked. A clean clear keeps you from arriving at the first objective a level short.
The lanes you fed can hold for a clear. That is what the kills were for.
check: Your level against his, and how much gold you hold unspent.
breaks: If your lead is already an item ahead of his, the tempo is yours; keep pressing before he catches up on farm.
basis: pro:An early gank is paid for in camps

asks: how do I path as Kayn
kayn second clear where
can I gank through walls
where do I gank from as kayn
say: Use Shadow Step to come through a wall behind the lane where they don't ward, or keep clearing if no wave is near your tower.
more: Walking through terrain means your gank route doesn't pass the usual river bushes, so the usual river wards often miss you.
It also lets you cut straight between camps, which saves walking time on the second clear.
Ganks from behind work best on a lane that has pushed past the middle.
check: Where the wave is, and whether the target still has Flash or a dash.
breaks: If the lane is pushed to their tower, a wall route only delivers you under it; clear instead.

asks: how do I path as ivern
ivern what do I do between camps
where do I go while groves grow
ivern second clear
say: Plant groves on every camp you pass, then go help a lane while they grow, or wait and free them if no lane needs you.
more: Ivern doesn't fight camps. The grove grows on its own time, so the minute after planting is free for a lane.
That makes your route a loop: plant, visit a lane with a shield or root, come back and collect.
Your allies can dash to a target you root, so pick the lane with a champion who wants to jump in.
check: Which groves are fully grown, and whether their jungler is nearby to take the camps you marked.
breaks: If their jungler is invading, he can simply kill a camp you left growing; collect before you leave that side.

asks: belveth where do I go
how do I stack as belveth
bel'veth second clear
should I gank or farm as belveth
say: Large monsters and takedowns both give you permanent attack speed, so keep clearing big camps, or take a skirmish you can win for the stack.
more: Your passive pays for every large monster and every champion takedown, so you lose little by choosing either.
What you can't afford is dead time. Walking between lanes with nothing to hit is the only path that gives no stacks.
Your ultimate needs Void coral on the ground to consume, so look around for it after a fight before you leave.
check: Which camps are up, and whether any Void coral is on the ground near you.
breaks: If their jungler is a level up, skirmishes are losing ones; stick to camps on the far side until you match him.

when: your health is low and you are level 4 or 5
asks: I'm low after clearing
low hp do I keep farming
can I take crab this low
half health where do I go
say: At this health a river fight is lost before it starts, so recall and come back to fresh camps, or take one safe camp first.
more: Their jungler only needs to find you once. A recall costs seconds, a death costs the whole next clear.
Recalling while your camps are down means you lose almost nothing; you walk back as they return.
If you hold gold for a component, the recall is paying for itself anyway.
check: Where their jungler last showed, and whether the camp nearest you is deep on your own side.
breaks: If their jungler is dead or just showed far away, finish the camps that are up before you go.

when: your mid laner is dead or has a respawn timer
asks: my mid just died can I still go river
mid's dead where do I path
is river safe
mid died do I contest
say: With your mid dead their mid walks to river first, so farm your own side, or cover the mid wave if no camp is up.
more: River fights go to whoever has the nearer lane arriving. Right now that is them.
Catching the mid wave under tower saves your laner's gold and experience and keeps you safe.
Go back to river once your mid is in lane again and has pushed.
check: Your mid's respawn timer, and whether their mid stayed in lane or went missing.
breaks: If their jungler is also dead, the river is open after all; take the crab or their near camps.
basis: pro:A low or dead enemy mid makes the river yours

when: their mid laner is dead or has a respawn timer
asks: their mid is dead what do I do
enemy mid died where do I go
mid's free now what
can I invade now
say: Their mid is down, so the river is yours: take the crab or step into their near camps, or start dragon if it's alive.
more: Nobody on their side can rotate first, even if they see you. That is priority without needing a wave.
Bring your mid along. Two of you in their jungle can also place the ward that covers the next objective.
The window ends when he walks back to lane, so choose one thing and finish it.
check: Whether a crab or dragon is actually alive, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If your own mid is low or recalled, you're alone in there; take only what's on your side of river.
basis: pro:A low or dead enemy mid makes the river yours

when: you and their jungler are the same level with similar CS
asks: we're even in jungle what do I do
same level as their jungler
how do I get ahead of him
even game where do I path
say: You're even, so path opposite to him and trade camps and ganks cross-map, or mirror him only if your lanes on that side push first.
more: Even junglers decide nothing by fighting each other. The lanes that arrive decide it.
Going opposite gives you uncontested ganks and makes him choose between covering and farming.
Mirroring is how you protect a lane he wants to dive, so do it for a reason.
check: Which side he last showed on, and which of your lanes has the wave moving forward.
breaks: If you can't tell where he is, opposite is a guess; take the side where your stronger lane is and ward on the way.

when: you are level 2 or 3 with a kill or assist, before 4:00
asks: I ganked early now what
skipped camps to gank where next
did a three camp gank what now
my other side is still up
say: Go straight back to the camps you skipped before he takes them, or recall first if the gank gave you gold for a component.
more: An early gank is paid for in camps. The half you left is open, and so is the far crab.
If your mid has push, the skipped side is safer and you can afford the recall.
Either way, expect to be slightly behind on level until those camps are cleared.
check: Which camps you skipped, whether your mid is pushed in, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If he already showed on your skipped side, don't walk in alone; take his opposite camps as the trade.
basis: pro:An early gank is paid for in camps

when: before 4:00
asks: which crab do I take
top crab or bot crab
should I go for scuttle
crab's spawning where do I go
say: Take the crab on the side where your lanes are pushing, or cross and take the other one if he's already there with help.
more: Both crabs spawn at 2:55. Early river fights are decided by which lanes walk over, not by the two junglers.
One crab each is a fine result. You lose nothing by declining a fight you would arrive second to.
The crab you take also tells him where you are, so expect him on the opposite side afterward.
check: Which mid and side waves are pushed, and who is already walking toward river.
breaks: If neither of your nearby lanes can move, skip both crabs and keep your camps on time.
basis: pro:Take the crab on the side where your lanes can move

when: before 4:00 and their jungler's item list changed before yours
asks: he backed before crab should I fight
their jungler has an item already
do I contest crab he's got a buy
he recalled early what now
say: He's back with an item, so don't duel him at that crab; take the other crab instead, or contest with a laner beside you.
more: A component at the first river meeting is a real edge in a one on one.
You don't have to accept the duel. He paid for that item with clear time, so you are ahead on camps for now.
Recall after your own clear and the gap closes by the next river fight.
check: Whether the second crab is alive, and which side he walked back to.
breaks: If your mid arrives first and his doesn't, numbers beat the item; take the fight with two.
basis: pro:A fast clear and recall brings an item to the river

when: between 2:55 and 4:00 and you are level 3
asks: I'm only level three can I take crab
ganked early do I go crab
level 3 crab or camps
short clear should I contest scuttle
say: At level three, leave the crab he's coming to and finish your camps, or take the far crab if he showed on the other side.
more: A full clear is about level four. Arriving at river a level short is the usual way a short clear gets punished.
Your skipped camps are worth more than a contested crab right now.
If your early gank got a kill, your laner can come with you. That changes the numbers.
check: His level compared with yours, and which crab is nearer to where he last showed.
breaks: If he is also level three because he ganked too, the crab fight is even; go by which lane can help.
basis: pro:Early on, a level is worth more than a little gold

asks: when does crab respawn
is there another scuttle
where's the next crab
why is there only one crab
say: After both first crabs die there's one crab, two and a half minutes later on a random side, so check river, or clear until it shows.
more: That means the single crab can't appear before about 5:25, and later if either first crab lived longer.
It tends to arrive just as junglers are close to level six, which is why it gets fought over.
Because the side is random, look at the map before you plan a route around it.
check: When the second of the first two crabs died, and which river side the new one appears on.
breaks: If one of the first crabs is still alive, there is no single crab yet; go and take that one.

when: you and their jungler are both level 5 and it is after 5:25
asks: do I fight for the single crab
we're both five is crab worth it
crab's up and he's coming
should I contest this scuttle
say: If that crab would finish your level six, keep hitting it through the fight and ult after; otherwise back off and let your lanes arrive first.
more: A monster in the middle of a skirmish is also experience. Sometimes the level it gives is the whole fight.
He can zone you off it, but that costs him abilities spent away from your teammates.
If you're further from six than he is, the same logic works against you, so don't start it.
check: How close you are to six, whether the crab is still alive, and who has an ultimate already.
breaks: If he is the one about to level from it, kill him or leave; standing near it at five against six loses.
basis: pro:A crab can be the level that wins the skirmish

when: you are level 5
asks: how do I get six fastest
I need level six quick
what's the quickest way to six
almost six what do I farm
say: Take whatever camps are up on the way to the crab for the fastest six, or gank now if a lane is ready and can't wait.
more: Camps are guaranteed experience. A gank that gets nothing sets your six back by the time it took.
The single crab often lands right when you need it, so glance at river before choosing your next camp.
Tell your lanes you are close. A gank a little later with your ultimate is usually the better one.
check: Which camps are alive, whether the crab is up, and how full your experience bar is.
breaks: If a lane is being dived right now, six can wait; a counter-gank at five with numbers still works.

when: you are level 6 and their jungler is level 5
asks: I hit six before him
I'm six he's five what do I do
how do I use six first
got my ult first now what
say: You have an ultimate and he doesn't, so gank with it now or fight him at his camps, or start dragon while he's a level down.
more: This window lasts only until he finishes a camp or two. Farming through it gives it back.
A gank with your ultimate against a lane his jungler can't match is the safest use.
If dragon is up, a level lead at the Smite fight is a strong reason to start it.
check: Whether your ultimate is actually ready, which lane has a wave you can use, and whether dragon is alive.
breaks: If your lanes are all pushed to their towers and no objective is up, take his camps instead so he stays five longer.
basis: pro:Do not fight an objective one spike behind

when: you are level 5 and their jungler is level 6
asks: he's six and I'm not
their jungler got six first
I'm five he's six do I fight
how do I play until I'm six
say: He has his ultimate and you don't, so farm to six on the far side, or shadow the lane he's most likely to dive.
more: One ultimate is the difference in an early skirmish. Give the crab rather than contest it a level down.
Ping your lanes that he is six. His next gank is the dangerous one.
If dragon is up and it isn't their soul point, it is cheaper to give than a lost fight. Take camps or a gank opposite.
check: How far you are from six, and which lane his champion's ultimate threatens most.
breaks: If his ultimate was just used in a fight you saw, the gap is gone for now; play as if you're even.
basis: pro:Do not fight an objective one spike behind

when: it is after 5:00 and you are still level 4
asks: I'm way behind on levels
still level four what do I do
should I even go for crab
I'm so behind in jungle
say: Skip the crab and take every camp you have without stopping, or gank only a lane that's right beside your route.
more: A full clear is about level four, so at this point you are a clear behind. Camps fix that faster than anything else.
Walking to a contested crab costs time and risks the death that puts you two clears behind.
Your lanes need to know you can't cover river for a couple of minutes.
check: Which camps are alive on both of your sides, and the enemy jungler's level.
breaks: If the enemy jungler is also level four, nobody is ahead; take the crab if your lanes can move.

when: you are level 5 or 6 and one of your laners is level 5
asks: should I wait for my laner to hit six
gank now or when mid is six
my mid's almost six
do I wait for their ult
say: Wait one wave and gank when your laner hits six for the kill, or go now if the enemy laner is about to hit six first.
more: Two ultimates on one target is a different gank from one. Solo lanes reach six around the same time you do.
The race cuts both ways. A gank before their laner gets his ultimate is easier than one after.
Use the waiting time on a camp next to that lane, not in the bush.
check: The enemy laner's level, and whether the wave will be on your side when the level arrives.
breaks: If the wave will be shoved to their tower by then, the level doesn't help; go now or pick another lane.
basis: pro:Early on, a level is worth more than a little gold

asks: crab or gank
lane's pinging me but crab is up
do I take scuttle or help bot
scuttle first or gank first
say: Gank first if the wave is near your tower, since the crab can wait, or take the crab if the lane is pushed up.
more: A good wave state lasts one wave. A crab stays until someone kills it.
The risk is their jungler taking the crab while you gank. That is a fair trade for a kill or a Flash.
If the gank works, bring the laner to the crab afterward.
check: Where the wave is right now, and whether their jungler could be at that crab already.
breaks: If the crab would give you level six, take it first; the gank is much stronger with your ultimate.

when: two or more of your teammates are dead
asks: team's dead can I take crab
do I contest crab alone
everyone died should I go river

Absolute Zero slows everyone who walks into the pit, which makes contesting you expensive.
